blocks.x: One governed door for every model call in the enterprise: the gateway, registry, prompt CI, guardrails, caching and spend controls that let fifty use cases share infrastructure without sharing incidents — or budgets.
The platform economics nobody prices until month three

The GenAI platform is the layer that makes every model call in the enterprise observable, bounded and cheap enough to survive finance. Gateway, registry, prompt CI, guardrails, caching, spend controls — none of it is glamorous, all of it decides whether the fifty use cases on the roadmap become real.

Without this layer, every team builds its own model plumbing: three vector stores, five prompt formats, no idea what anything costs. With it, a new use case is configuration plus an eval suite — and the platform team holds p95 latency and cost per 1k calls the way SREs hold availability.
The sections below are the platform build order: failure modes first, then the reference architecture, then the console that keeps the platform honest in production.
Four ways GenAI platforms blow their mandate
Platforms fail politically before they fail technically — these four failure modes are why internal platforms get bypassed, and the countermeasures that keep teams on the governed path.

widgets.title: The platform rails — click nodes for the shared contract

nodes.label: PII screen
nodes.detail: Edge screening with entity policy per region; blocked payloads regenerate in-region rather than leaking cross-border.

nodes.label: Model gateway
nodes.detail: Routing, fallbacks, quotas, spend accounting and caching — the single entry point for every model call in the estate.

nodes.label: Prompt registry
nodes.detail: Versioned prompts with eval scores per version; a prompt change ships like code — reviewed, scored, roll-back-able.

nodes.label: Retrieval catalogue
nodes.detail: Indices with freshness SLAs, source lineage and access scopes; retrieval quality is measured, not assumed.

nodes.label: Policy & safety layer
nodes.detail: Commitment rules, refusal policies and output screens — evidence stored per decision for the audit story.

nodes.label: Serving classes
nodes.detail: Latency-classed serving lanes (interactive, batch, bulk); interactive traffic never queues behind a batch job.

nodes.label: Eval harness
nodes.detail: Golden cases per feature; nightly scores published on the platform scoreboard; regressions block deploys.

nodes.label: Observability
nodes.detail: Traces with prompt, retrieval, model, cost and policy outcome per call — the debugging surface for every team.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read the shared contract each rail offers. Teams inherit all eight rails by onboarding — none of them re-solve inference or safety alone.

blocks.x: Default platform components — and the deviations we allow

The default stack optimizes for operability with a small senior team; each deviation condition is a written trigger, so choosing differently is a documented decision rather than an accumulation of exceptions.

blocks.caption: Generative AI Platform Engineering: default stack and the conditions under which we deviate
rows: Gateway
Envoy-based or dedicated LLM gateway with typed use-case keys
Thin proxy only when a vendor-native feature is genuinely irreplaceable
Registry
Model + prompt + eval triplet pinned immutably
Git-only registry is acceptable below ~20 use cases, with CI enforcement
Guardrails
Inline classification stack: injection, PII, topic, output schema
Post-hoc sampling only for internal low-risk tiers — never for regulated surfaces
Caching
Semantic cache with similarity threshold + TTL per use case
Exact-match cache for deterministic workloads like classification
Hosting
Vendor APIs default; self-hosted for residency or cost at scale
Self-hosting a frontier-class model without a residency or unit-cost case
Observability
OpenTelemetry end-to-end with cost dimensions on every span
Sampling at 100% for regulated use cases, 10% elsewhere

blocks.x: The platform build, sprint by sprint

items: Weeks 1–2 — estate & baseline
Inventory existing model calls and spend; define use-case manifest schema; sign latency and cost targets
Weeks 3–5 — gateway core
Authz, metering, tracing and budgets behind one SDK; egress policy fail-closed
Weeks 6–7 — registry & prompt CI
Triplet pinning, eval CI on merge, rollback drill
Weeks 8–9 — guardrails & cache
Inline guard stack per data class; semantic cache with per-use-case thresholds
Weeks 10–12 — migration & drills
Move existing calls behind the gateway tier by tier; failover and 2× load drills
Ongoing — platform product
Roadmap-driven golden paths; quarterly cost and latency target review

blocks.x: Governance enforced once, inherited by every consuming team

Platform-level controls multiply across every consuming use case, which is exactly why they are enforced once, here — injection scanning, egress policy, key vaulting and per-domain budget enforcement.
